relations.myth: Offerings travel by river through Mamacocha to the Creator
relations.note: River-borne sacrifices could reach the Creator through or within Mamacocha.
relations.source: Molina, Relación de las fábulas y ritos

relations.myth: Catalogue of worshipped earth and sea powers
relations.note: Acosta lists Pachamama and Mamacocha successively as worshipped natural powers.
relations.source: Acosta, Historia natural y moral V.4

relations.myth: Terrestrial and marine fields in the Coricancha cosmogram
relations.note: Pachamama and Mama Cocha occupy corresponding terrestrial and marine positions.
Acosta compares Mamacocha to Tethys through European classical interpretation.
relations.source: Acosta, Historia natural y moral V.4

relations.note: Acosta compares Mamacocha to Neptune through European classical interpretation.
relations.source: Acosta, Historia natural y moral V.4

relations.myth: Sequential Huacho shoreline and guano-island rites
relations.note: Travelers offered chicha beside the sea, then worshipped Huamancántac on the islands.
